reason: The text of Exodus 14 demonstrates precisely the opposite of the statement. God performs a miraculous salvation specifically for the people (בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל), not just the leaders. When the people cry out in fear, God responds with direct action by parting the Red Sea to save them from the Egyptian army. God explicitly tells Moses to speak to the people to advance (דַּבֵּ֥ר אֶל־ בְּנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְיִסָּֽעוּ), and orchestrates their deliverance with detailed instructions. The climax emphasizes that 'the Lord saved Israel that day from the hand of the Egyptians' (וַיּ֨וֹשַׁע יְהוָ֜ה בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֛וּא אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵל), and the people's response is to believe in the Lord and develop reverence. This narrative arc demonstrates God's empathy and care extending to the entire people, not merely leaders.
